purpose: Vandetanib is used to treat a rare type of thyroid cancer called medullary thyroid cancer that has spread to other parts of the body and cannot be removed by surgery. It works best for adults whose cancer is getting worse or causing symptoms. Your doctor will decide if this medicine is right for your specific situation.
how_it_works: Think of cancer cells as having special 'on switches' called receptors that help them grow and spread. Vandetanib works by blocking several of these switches at the same time, which slows down or stops the cancer cells from growing and forming new blood vessels to feed themselves. By turning off these signals, the medicine helps keep the cancer under better control.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, rash or skin changes, tiredness, high blood pressure, headache, loss of appetite, stomach pain, and sensitivity to sunlight are among the most common side effects. Some people also notice dry skin or changes in their nails.
warnings: This medicine can cause a serious heart rhythm problem called QT prolongation, which can be life-threatening — your doctor will monitor your heart with regular EKGs. It can also cause severe skin reactions, vision problems, and lung inflammation. Vandetanib can harm an unborn baby, so effective birth control is very important during and for several months after treatment. Because of serious risks, this medication is only available through a special program called REMS, and not every pharmacy can dispense it.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 300 mg taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. If you miss a dose and it is less than 12 hours before your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule — never take two doses at once.
